newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Share trading in Nigerian Coke bottler on hold.
newsitem.headline: Share trading in Nigerian Coke bottler on hold.

text.p: Trading in the shares of Coca-cola bottlers in Nigeria was suspended on Wednesday over a possible merger plan, the stock exchange said.
"Nigerian Bottling Company is involved in a possible corporate arrangement which the Nigerian Stock Exchange is not informed of," an official of the exchange told Reuters.

Traders said the supsension followed a newspaper report on Monday that the company planned to pay 1.2 billion naira to acquire a firm in Aba, eastern Nigeria which currently bottles its brands under an agreement.
The report said the firm, Sapanda Industries Ltd, was expected to become a wholly-owned subsidiary of Nigerian Bottling Company.
Company officials could not be reached immediately for comments.
"The shares will remain suspended until there is an explanation from the company," the exchange official said.
Nigerian Bottling Company announced a six percent increase in after-tax profits to end-June on Monday.
It netted 678.9 million naira in the six months against 637.8 million in the same period of 1995.
An undisclosed minority interest further cut profit after tax by 47.6 million naira compared to 22.1 million in the same period of last year.
Its shares rose 13 kobo to 28.72 naira following Monday's result announcement. ($1=80 naira)
